newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army pushes deeper into rebel territory.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army pushes deeper into rebel territory.

text.p: Sri Lankan army troops pushed deeper into rebel-held northern territory on Thursday after advancing some nine km (six miles) virtually unopposed over two days, a military spokesman said.

Liberation Tigers of Tamil Ealam (LTTE) guerrillas had so far offered little resistance to the army march from the frontline town of Vavuniya, in north-central Sri Lanka, towards the northwest costal town of Mannar, he said.
On Wednesday, the Defence Ministry said the LTTE had abandoned two camps in the path of the offensive, which is led by elite commando and air-mobile units.
Colombo newspapers described the push, code-named "Edibala" (brave force), as the government's biggest anti-guerrilla operation this year.
The LTTE said an air force Pucara ground attack aircraft fired three missiles at civilians in rebel-held areas near the strategic town of Kilinochchi causing casualties.
The LTTE statement, published on their Internet web site, did not give details.
Sri Lanka's military says it does not deliberately target civilians and that any civilian casualties are accidents.
Some military officials said the army was trying to link Vavuniya and Kilinochchi, 70 km (50 miles) to Vavuniya's north.
Other military officials said the army's aim was to clear a supply route to Mannar after intelligence reports of a rebel build-up in the area.
Defence analysts said the objective could be Kilinochchi as part of an effort to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula and ultimately link Colombo with the entire northern part of the island.

Kilinochchi has been the focus of recent fighting. Its only current supply route is a road linking it to Jaffna on the northern tip of the Indian Ocean island. Jaffna itself can only be supplied by air or sea.

The LTTE's statement also accused the government of rounding up more than 50 Tamil youths in Colombo and its suburbs on Tuesday, Sri Lanka's independence day, under the draconian Prevention of Terrorism Act.
Military officials have said roundups are a routine security measure to prevent rebel infiltration of the capital and that most detainees are freed after questioning.

The LTTE has been fighting for a separate Tamil homeland in the country's north and east since 1983. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the conflict but the LTTE says the toll is much higher.
